details:
ASTRA HEALTH is an AI-powered astronaut health monitoring platform designed to improve the safety and well-being of astronauts during long-duration space missions. It addresses major spaceflight health challenges, including radiation exposure, isolation, confinement, altered gravity, bone loss, cardiovascular changes, immune system disturbances, and behavioral health problems.

The platform works by collecting health indicators such as heart rate, blood pressure, blood oxygen, sleep quality, physical activity, stress levels, and mood. It can also integrate medical examination results, bone density measurements, immune system indicators, and radiation exposure records. Artificial intelligence analyzes these data, establishes a personalized health baseline for each astronaut, detects unusual patterns, and identifies potential health risks. An AI Health Copilot explains detected changes and provides recommendations based on approved medical guidance. Other features include an Early Warning Center, mental health monitoring, health reports, and a Space Health Digital Twin that tracks health changes over time.

The main benefit is enabling astronauts to recognize potential health problems earlier, understand their physical and psychological condition, and make informed decisions without depending entirely on immediate medical assistance from Earth. The platform also supports medical teams by organizing health records and presenting meaningful trends. Its offline-first design allows essential monitoring and alerts to continue when communication with Earth is unavailable.

Our intended impact is to make long-duration space missions safer by transforming health measurements into practical insights that support continuous health management and early intervention. In the future, ASTRA HEALTH could support missions to the Moon and Mars, where access to medical facilities is limited.

The planned development tools include HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Python, React, Next.js, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, Pandas, NumPy, and Scikit-learn. Data visualization libraries will present health trends, while machine learning models will support anomaly detection and predictive analysis. The initial prototype will use simulated astronaut health data, with future integration planned for wearable sensors and specialized medical devices.

The creative aspect of ASTRA HEALTH is its combination of personalized monitoring, predictive artificial intelligence, and Digital Twin technology in one platform. Instead of displaying isolated measurements, it examines relationships between different health indicators and provides understandable explanations. Our team considered scientific accuracy, astronaut safety, usability, data privacy, limited communication, hardware limitations, and the need to distinguish between simulated information and real medical measurements. The system is designed as a medical decision-support tool, not a replacement for professional diagnosis.
